body:
Releasing the claim on the setup sheet's two closed doors. Product commit 0ba95d9.

What was wrong, and reproduced rather than inferred. Escape was ignored whenever the focus sat in a text
field, and the sheet's ✕ scrolled out of reach once the content exceeded the sheet's 598px cap. Both exits
dead at once, in the one state a person is in when they want out. Driven in a real window on its own debug
port and profile: sheet open with focus in a text field, a real Escape through CDP's Input domain, still
open; the same press with the focus anywhere else closed it. Geometry: content overflowed by 86px at
1280x720, and scrolling to the bottom put the close button at top:-23 — three pixels remaining.

What shipped. `escapeDismisses` in `core/nav.ts` — the rule now lives beside the transitions that already
own the sheet, and it keeps the promise that file's own comment already made ("Esc closes them"). Two things
may take Escape first: an IME mid-composition, and an open `select`. Seven new assertions in `nav.test.ts`
hold the logic half down. `.drawer-bar` is sticky, with its spacing moved from margin to padding and a
matching shadow so nothing scrolls through the strip above it.

Found by sweeping for the same class, and worse: nothing bounded the confirmer's height. `.dialog` had no
ceiling, the scrim centres what cannot fit, so a long proposed action took Deny and Allow off the bottom of
the window with no scroll to reach them — a run blocked on an answer whose buttons are unreachable. Measured
with the same markup carrying the real classes: 851px dialog in a 720px viewport with the foot outside it
before, capped with only the body scrolling after.

Verified, and what the evidence is. A screenshot read, not just a number: scrolled to the bottom the bar is
still at the top of the sheet and no content bleeds past it; at rest the geometry is byte-for-byte what it
was, so nothing looks different when you are not scrolled. pre-commit PASSED (renderer 179 assertions,
typecheck, sidecar 44). `html` eslint-free, typecheck clean.

Honest limit on the dialog half: I could not drive a real confirmer — it needs a mutating world plus a model
that proposes one, and none is reachable here — so that half is a geometry proof on the real stylesheet with
synthesized markup of the same structure, not a driven dialog. Stated rather than glossed.

Not claimed as fixed, and not a defect: the supervisor's second question, being asked for the API key again
each launch. Everything but the key's value is persisted; the value is session-only by deliberate design, and
the intended way around it (an env var, which the sidecar inherits) already exists. Raised as
P-2026-09-26-1 for the supervisor, because storing a credential is a security decision and not mine.

Files touched: app/renderer/core/nav.ts, app/renderer/core/nav.test.ts,
app/renderer/shell/ConfigDrawer.tsx, app/renderer/styles.css. Safe to touch all four now.
